new_findings.title: ias-executor-ts submodule pointer not advanced — 3 commits untracked by super-repo
new_findings.description: Super-repo commits 34c55690 and d42c4fd1 describe changes to ias-executor-ts (commits 37a9ddb and b6b58a2) but do NOT advance the super-repo submodule pointer. The pointer remains at 49bfb432a8684ae25e0bbb7eb0c48773846bc3dd (2026-05-26T19:45Z) while the submodule HEAD is at b6b58a2074d9b6b66468c4d293d846a7f8ce66c8 (3 commits ahead: 161eede, 37a9ddb, b6b58a2).
sub_findings: verify-dist-fresh.ts (b6b58a2) exists locally in repos/ias-executor-ts/scripts/ but NOT in the container (/vessels/ias-executor-ts has only dist/, src/, node_modules/ — no scripts/ dir). The script is a developer tool meant to run from the operator's workspace, not from inside the container. This is expected design, but means F-111 closure is a workspace-tool only — the tool prevents future drift if used; it does not detect or prevent past drift autonomously.

The async resolveInputs with poll-and-wait (37a9ddb) IS deployed in the container dist (verified: /vessels/ias-executor-ts/dist/engine.js contains EXECUTOR_INPUT_RESOLUTION_TIMEOUT_MS logic). The functional change is live even though the pointer is stale.

ias-executor-ts remote origin (git@github.com:AviGopal/ias-executor-ts.git) returns 'Repository not found'. The 3 new commits have no remote backup. A container rebuild or git submodule update would lose these commits from the workspace (the deployed dist in the container would survive, but the source history would be orphaned).
new_findings.risk: No remote backup for 3 functional commits. Container rebuild does not restore source; dist rebuild from stale pointer (49bfb43) would revert async resolveInputs behavior to pre-37a9ddb state.
new_findings.recommendation: Push ias-executor-ts to a recoverable remote (or mirror). Advance super-repo submodule pointer to b6b58a2. Until then, avoid git submodule update on repos/ias-executor-ts.

new_findings.title: Promote guard allowlist includes CI/deployment resolvers absent from single-container substrate
new_findings.description: The hardcoded builtInResolvers set in activities.ts promote endpoint includes helmfile_sync, scaffold_vessel_skeleton, docker_build_push. These are CI/deployment-context resolvers not registered in the single-container substrate's discovery registry. Templates using these resolvers will pass the promote guard but fail at execution time. This is a false-negative window in the guard — permissive by design for multi-substrate compatibility, but the substrate cannot execute such templates if promoted.
new_findings.risk: LOW — templates using these resolvers are unlikely to be authored by the substrate's own proposal system (which should only reference registered resolvers). The promote guard still catches hallucinated arbitrary names. The primary risk is that a substrate-authored proposal using helmfile_sync would pass promotion silently.
new_findings.recommendation: Consider warning (not refusing) when built-in resolver is not in discovery registry — provides observability without breaking multi-substrate compat.
